searchText: should we just normalize this ot [host](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/host) or [hostname](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/hostname), maybe having port part of it could be useful for testing but why do we need to sign over the scheme and other parts of the url? also related, I mentioned the trailing slash problem here already https://github.com/JasonVranek/epbs-config-flow/pull/1#discussion_r3789290387 <@346498651553660928> might be able to write here, there is a discord glitch that allows to write in threads I think, or maybe it's just a misconfig on this server yea agree with Nico, so hex-encoded UTF-8 bytes of the builder's ***[host](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/host)*** ? and to be explicit, since the auth data contains opaque bytes, a builder can check any encoding / agree with proposers out-of-protocol on encodings. this ^ should be how VCs create normalized auth data from the `url` iff a user doesn't supply auth data directly via keymanager API for that builder https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-host seems fine to me, <@755590043632140352> since you the one adding trailing slashes for no good reason to your builder urls, what do you prefer? https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/168 decided hostname is better, for local testing if it's really and issue, can just ignore auth, or define custom auth data cc <@808969530608451584> this would require buildoor updates

excerpts.author: jvranek
excerpts.content:
yea agree with Nico, so hex-encoded UTF-8 bytes of the builder's ***[host](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/host)*** ?

and to be explicit, since the auth data contains opaque bytes, a builder can check any encoding / agree with proposers out-of-protocol on encodings. this ^ should be how VCs create normalized auth data from the `url` iff a user doesn't supply auth data directly via keymanager API for that builder

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-host seems fine to me, <@755590043632140352> since you the one adding trailing slashes for no good reason to your builder urls, what do you prefer?
